SYMPTOM: `XCTAssertNotNil(Settings.load().userEmail)` fails right after `Settings.save(settings)` — load() returns old data
CAUSE: `Settings.save()` dispatches work to `SettingsPersistenceActor` via a fire-and-forget `Task {}` and returns immediately. The save hasn't completed when the assertion runs.
FIX: In tests, use XCTestExpectation + small delay, or just verify the in-memory state instead of the persisted state:
  ```swift
  let exp = expectation(description: "save")
  Task {
    await Task.yield()  // let save Task execute
    exp.fulfill()
  }
  await fulfillment(of: [exp], timeout: 1.0)
  ```
Alternatively, test the settings object directly rather than round-tripping through save/load.
PREVENT: Never assert synchronously after Settings.save() — it's async by design via SettingsPersistenceActor
